column1: # The rust front's features that std2's items wait for: each one code,
# gaps the real check shows (typecheck.txt), named for ed270, with the
# release ed270 gave each (`-`: none yet). A column NAME, the release it
# lands in, what it is. Read by tools/std2-checklist.py.

column3: the char type; 'x' is a u8 in 0.27.0, so `impl char` waits too
FnOnce as a bound
`impl .. for &'a T`
Index through SliceIndex, its `?Sized` Output
bounds on an associated type's declaration
`<X as Tr>::Name`
a type parameter inferred from the expected result, beyond bidirectional checking
associated consts
a blanket impl beside specific ones (Rust's coherence)
auto traits as bounds (compiler-known structural markers)
derives emitting Rust's shapes (PartialEq, Hash<H>, Debug through Formatter)
compiler-known assert, format, write and writeln: the format literal at a call
an inherent impl on an instantiation (Option<&'a T>)
an item over [T; N] for every N, compiler-provided until const generics (plan §6): `#[array_builtin(N)]`
a trait's impls for the primitive types, compiler-provided as MVS's are: `#[builtin_impls(i8, ..., bool)]` on the trait
a where clause's bound on a projection or another type than a parameter
a trait's supertraits (`trait Eq: PartialEq`)
tuple structs (`struct Reverse<T>(pub T)`)
an impl's parameter that only the trait's arguments or a bound's projection fix (`impl<T> SliceIndex<[T]> for usize`, `impl<B, I, F: FnMut(I::Item) -> B> Iterator for Map<I, F>`)
two impls of one generic trait for one type (`AsRef<str>` and `AsRef<[u8]>` for str): the second is checked against the first's signature
a default body in a generic trait (`PartialEq<Rhs>::ne`)
two traits' methods of one name on a type, or a trait's and an inherent one (`Debug::fmt` and `Display::fmt`, `Iterator::eq` and `PartialEq::eq`)
not the front's: std2 checked as a root still loads MVS's std (its prelude, its primitives' methods, its by-value parameters); it goes when std2 becomes the std in 0.27.2
`mem::size_of` and `mem::align_of`, the builtins' names
`&self[..mid]` on a `&str`: read as slicing a raw pointer
a unit struct's name as its value (`PhantomData`)
`self` in a use list (`use super::hash_map::{self, HashMap}`)
`unsafe fn(..)` pointer types
`&&'a T` (the lexer's `&&`), a front bug
`?` on std2's Result and Option (Z3: the compiler-known items re-pointed at the switch)
`&mut [u8] as *mut [u8] as *mut str` and the other fat-pointer casts (Z9)
